tasks.details:
Create `data_layer/metrics/financial_period.py` with:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date
from typing import Literal
from enum import Enum

class QualityFlag(str, Enum):
    OK = 'OK'
    PARTIAL = 'PARTIAL'
    INSUFFICIENT_DATA = 'INSUFFICIENT_DATA'

class AdoptionMethod(str, Enum):
    FULL_RETROSPECTIVE = 'FULL_RETROSPECTIVE'
    MODIFIED_RETROSPECTIVE = 'MODIFIED_RETROSPECTIVE'
    UNKNOWN = 'UNKNOWN'

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class LineItem:
    value: float | None
    unit: str
    source_tag: str
    source_accession: str
    quality_flag: QualityFlag
    
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FinancialPeriod:
    cik: int
    fiscal_year: int
```

tasks.title: Implement ASC 606 Adoption Method Detection
tasks.description: Extend FinancialPeriodAssembler to detect whether a company used full or modified retrospective adoption for ASC 606 revenue recognition standard. Flag series comparability accordingly.
tasks.details:
Add method `_detect_asc606_adoption()` to FinancialPeriodAssembler:

Detection algorithm (BINARY, no thresholds per PRD):
1. Identify transition year: first fiscal year where RevenueFromContractWithCustomer* tag appears
2. In the transition year filing, check if NEW tag has values for periods BEFORE transition year
   - YES -> FULL_RETROSPECTIVE (prior periods were restated)
   - NO -> MODIFIED_RETROSPECTIVE (prior periods kept old tag)
3. If both tags exist for same period: record BOTH values, flag ANY discrepancy (no magnitude threshold)
4. Ambiguous cases -> UNKNOWN, treated as MODIFIED for safety

Set `FinancialPeriod.adoption_method` based on detection.
Set `is_comparable_to_prior = False` for the transition year if method is MODIFIED_RETROSPECTIVE or UNKNOWN.

Store dual values when both old and new tags exist:
```python
if old_tag_value and new_tag_value:
    items['revenue'] = LineItem(..., quality_flag=QualityFlag.PARTIAL)
    items['revenue_asc605'] = LineItem(old_value, ...)
    items['revenue_asc606'] = LineItem(new_value, ...)
```

No threshold for discrepancy flagging - ANY difference between old and new tag gets recorded. Distribution analysis happens on golden set in T4, not in code.

tasks.title: Implement Fiscal Year Change and Stub Period Detection
tasks.description: Extend FinancialPeriodAssembler to detect fiscal year changes (via 10-KT form or duration anomaly) and correctly flag stub periods. Only flow items are flagged; balance sheet items are unaffected.
tasks.details:
Add method `_detect_stub_period()` to FinancialPeriodAssembler:

Detection signals (use BOTH, either triggers investigation):
1. `period_end - period_start` outside 350-380 days for duration facts
2. `form = '10-KT'` (transition period annual report)

Handling:
- When stub period detected, set `FinancialPeriod.is_stub_period = True`
- ONLY flag FLOW items (those with period_start IS NOT NULL): revenue, ocf, net_income, etc.
- DO NOT flag INSTANT items (period_start IS NULL): assets, liabilities, equity, cash, debt positions
  - Balance sheet is point-in-time, independent of period length
  - Flagging them creates false PARTIAL and pollutes percentiles

YoY comparison rules (to be enforced in metrics layer):
- YoY loses TWO comparisons: into stub period AND out of stub period
- First comparable growth = second full year after change
- Example: FY2019 (12mo) -> FY2020-stub (6mo) -> FY2020 (12mo) -> FY2021 (12mo)
  - FY2020 growth vs FY2019: INVALID (comparing 12mo to 6mo)
  - FY2021 growth vs FY2020: INVALID (stub period base)
  - FY2022 growth vs FY2021: VALID (first comparable)

Store duration metadata for downstream use:
```python
FinancialPeriod.stub_duration_days = actual_duration  # if stub
FinancialPeriod.prior_fy_end_month = detected_old_fy_end  # for context
```
